questions: Should the server time appended to the echoed data be the exact time when the data was received, or the time when it is sent back (or something else)?
What should happen if the client sends data that is larger than buffer_size? Should it be truncated, split across multiple messages, or handled differently?
Is the server expected to handle multiple clients concurrently, and if so, should the time appended be per-client or global?
What should the server do if sending a response fails (e.g., due to a broken connection)? Should it close the socket, retry, or ignore?
Should the server's status message include any information about the number of clients served or errors encountered?
What encoding should be used for decoding received data and encoding sent data? Is UTF-8 always correct, or should it handle other encodings/errors?
Should the server handle signals or interrupts (e.g., KeyboardInterrupt) gracefully, and if so, how?
Is the server expected to log or print anything to stdout/stderr during operation, or only return the final status string?
